📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that amazon has cut prices across its entire Fire TV Soundbar lineup in this early Black Friday sale, with discounts covering everything from a basic two-channel soundbar designed to improve on your TV's built-in speakers to a full 5.1-channel setup with a wireless subwoofer and rear surround speakers. For more on the sale, you can also check out our Black Friday deals page, where we're covering the latest discounts ahead of this year's event.

Sources indicate that amazon Fire TV Soundbar is $74.99 (was $119.99), making it the least expensive option in the lineup for anyone who wants a step up from TV speakers for everyday viewing—it's a 24-inch, two-channel bar that supports DTS Virtual:X and Dolby Audio, though it doesn’t have Dolby Atmos or a separate subwoofer. Despite its name, it's an audio-only soundbar and requires a Fire TV streaming stick for you to get any of the Fire TV experience. For more on this soundbar, read PCMag’s review.

It has been revealed that amazon Fire TV Soundbar Plus is down to $139.99 from $249.99, and the extra money over the base model gets you a dedicated center channel that helps make dialogue easier to follow, along with a built-in subwoofer, Dolby Atmos, and DTS:X support. That noted, it doesn’t have up-firing drivers, so the Atmos effect stays largely horizontal, but the center channel does real work on mumbled dialogue in prestige dramas. As with the base model, this one also handles audio only and needs a Fire TV device for any of the streaming features. This PCMag review has more detail on how it performs.

Amazon Fire TV Soundbar with Alexa Voice Remote Pro is $109.98 (was $154.98). This pairs the entry-level bar with the upgraded remote, which adds backlit buttons, two customizable shortcuts you can set for favorite apps or Alexa commands, and a remote finder (for when it inevitably disappears into the couch). If you don’t specifically want or need the remote, though, the Soundbar Plus is a more capable soundbar for just $30 more.

It has been revealed that amazon Fire TV Soundbar Plus with Subwoofer is $229.99, down from $374.99. This configuration takes the same 3.1-channel bar and pairs it with a separate wireless subwoofer, which gives bass-heavy scenes and film scores considerably more weight than the bar's built-in woofer can manage on its own—and at $90 more than the discounted Soundbar Plus, this is the option I'd consider if fuller bass is a priority. Keep in mind that it doesn't add rear speakers, so you're still working with a 3.1 setup and sound that stays in front of you.

It has been revealed that amazon Fire TV Soundbar Plus with Subwoofer and Surround Sound Speakers is $349.99, down from $489.99. This is the complete 5.1 package, adding two rear speakers to the 3.1 bar and wireless subwoofer, so action scenes and other surround effects come from behind you, rather than only from the direction of the TV—but it costs $120 more than the discounted soundbar and subwoofer bundle, so it’s worth considering how much you want that surround-sound effect. Also, while the rear speakers connect to the soundbar wirelessly, each still needs a power outlet.

Sources indicate that in short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

According to recent reports, yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

No. If you find the product you're looking for with a major discount right now, get it. It's not likely to drop any lower, but it could always run out of stock. Take advantage of price matching or guarantees instead of waiting. Remember, you can always return products later if you change your mind. For the majority of products, the deal from Black Friday will be the same one on Cyber Monday.

Case in point: a content creator who has also worked on large communication towers was recently stunned by GTA 6′s attention to detail. Folks, we got Erathed tower legs.

Content creator MrMcg92, who primarily plays first-person shooters and military sims, is also someone who has, in real life, worked on and climbed large communication and radio towers. So whenever he comes across a radio tower in a video game, he takes some time to do a “Tower Inspection.” He’s looked at towers in Battlefield, Days Gone, and Far Cry. And while all of these towers had some nice details, they often made mistakes or were missing notable bits MrMcg92 would expect to find on a real comms tower. That wasn’t the case when he did a tower inspection in GTA 6. Instead, he was flabbergasted and impressed by the tower’s hyper-realistic details.

It has been revealed that “Oh my fucking god, boys,” exclaimed MrMcg92 when walking up to a radio tower in GTA 6. “For the first time ever, we got the tower legs earthed. Earthed tower legs with saddles. And double locknuts on the HDs, lads. Double lock nuts everywhere!”.

He then spotted a red power cable running up the middle of the tower and claimed that if there was an aircraft warning light at the top, he would get a “stiffy.”Â As he climbed the tower, he continued to be impressed by how Rockstar’s artists included every tiny detail that should be found on a real-life tower like this.

In a recent development, “Oh, boys, we got proper AA clamps on the mount points. Tails running out the bottom of the panels to the RRU,” pointed out the creator on his climb up the tower. I don’t really know what half of this means, but based on his past videos, expert knowledge, and excitement, I get the feeling this is all just very, very impressive.

And yes, at the top was indeed a red warning light.

According to recent reports, I hope somewhere an artist at Rockstar who helped with this tower sees this video and gets to feel really proud of what they made. I can’t wait for more experts in code and utility regulations to start posting videos about how accurate GTA 6′s electrical cables and highways are, and I’m not even joking.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tasha Suri, author of the Burning Kingdoms trilogy and several other books, will be writing Baldur's Gate 3: Shadowheart, the official BG3books website has declared. Another prequel to Larian's videogame, this one focuses on Shadowheart's time as a priestess in the Church of Shar, and is about a murder mystery.

"When a member of their order is killed in the Upper City," the blurb goes, "Shadowheart and her so-called allies are called to investigate. She trusts none of them: not Mirie, the ambitious Griefguard; not Caldan, the cynical propagandist; and certainly not Nocturne, the charming quartermistress, who claims to have only Shadowheart’s best interests in mind.".

Recent findings suggest that mirie and Nocturne are both characters you can meet in Baldur's Gate 3, while Caldan Darkwood is mentioned in a note you can find. Nocturne in particular has a close relationship with Shadowheart, which could be interesting to see developed. "Torn between the familiar comforts of the dark and the thrill of new desire," the blurb continues, "she must solve the mystery to prove her devotion… or be cast into the light.".

Which sounds fine and dandy, but it'll have an uphill battle with the Baldur's Gate 3 fandom, who've been vocally critical of the Astarion novel for its lightness of tone—especially given his traumatic backstory—and apparently mischaracterizing Astarion and his sire, Cazador, as well as being inaccurate to the lore.

Industry observers note that I haven't read the Astarion book, but I did read the original Baldur's Gate novels, which were terrible. So were almost all the D&D books I read in a youthful post-Tolkien haze where I'd put up with anything that had wizards in it. My expectations are pretty low, but I do like to slip a trashy fantasy novel between heavier reads as a palate-cleanser so maybe I'll try this one some day.

Sources indicate that baldur's Gate 3: Shadowheart will be out in a 304-page hardcover edition and in ebook form on June 8, as well as a 10-hour audiobook. The Astarion audiobook was read by Astarion performer Neil Newbon, we'll have to wait and see if Jennifer English reads the Shadowheart book.

If the series continues I could see a Wyll prequel being interesting, since he gets a bit short-changed in the videogame, though I wouldn't expect it to sell as well as novels about the more popular companions.

  • Posting on Twitter/X on Friday evening, DerrickGott007 said they had "just got a 30-day PSN social features ban" for sending the photo, which they'd taken with the in-game camera, through PlayStation's messaging service, warning other players not to do the same.
  • "Do not, I repeat do not send any photos taken with the in-game camera, across the PSN messaging network that contain nudity," they wrote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Grand Theft Auto 6 player says they've been hit with a 30-day PlayStation Network ban after sending a friend a photo they took in the game's nudist resort.

Posting on Twitter/X on Friday evening, DerrickGott007 said they had "just got a 30-day PSN social features ban" for sending the photo, which they'd taken with the in-game camera, through PlayStation's messaging service, warning other players not to do the same.

"Do not, I repeat do not send any photos taken with the in-game camera, across the PSN messaging network that contain nudity," they wrote. "I just got a 30-day PSN social features ban for sending my friend a photo of the nudist colony in GTA6 that I found.".

In a screenshot of the notice, PlayStation Safety indicates that content sent from the player's account via Message on PlayStation "breached the Code of Conduct", and that their account has been "temporarily suspended from using PlayStation social features for 30 days" due to "pornographic or obscene content". It also warns that "further offenses may result in temporary or permanent suspension from the whole of PlayStation, not just social features".

PlayStation's Code of Conduct asks players not to "share, solicit, access, distribute or store material that is obscene, pornographic or illegal", and indicates Sony "may take any action as reasonably necessary to protect PlayStation and our players".

Recent findings suggest that DO NOT, I REPEAT DO NOT SEND ANY PHOTOS TAKEN WITH THE IN GAME CAMERA , ACROSS THE PSN MESSAGING NETWORK THAT CONTAIN NUDITY. I JUST GOT A 30 DAY PSN SOCIAL FEATURES BAN FOR SENDING MY FRIEND A PHOTO OF THE NUDIST COLONY IN GTA6 THAT I FOUND. pic.twitter.com/vsoIjmpGrt.

It has been revealed that crucially, as Dexerto points out, the code does not make an exception for content taken from games, even ones rated for adults. So if you've snapped anything cheeky in Leonida - say, full-frontal nudity in its nudist resort - you might want to keep it to yourself.

GTA 6 launched on Thursday, 19th November, for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, and while it's one of the best-reviewed games of all time, you wouldn't know it from its Metacritic user score, as players review bomb it over its limited FPS and purported "woke" agenda.

Spoilers below Who could it be now? In one of the later missions, players accompany Boobie on one of his errands. Once they reach a new club, Boobie meets up with Significant Mike and throws a few jibes at the local help sweeping the floor. That "little Santa" with the broom? None other than Rockstar Games president Sam Houser, who doesn't speak a single word in his brief appearance. Beyond minor background pedestrian and gangster voice roles in San Andreas and GTA 4, Houser has generally kept a low profile, focusing instead on developing the studio's games. "This is a narrative set in a world of possibilities--and it is up to you as the player to shape how it ultimately feels and concludes," he noted. Meanwhile, Houser's brother, Dan Houser, is working on an open-world comedy game at Absurd Ventures, the studio he founded after leaving Rockstar Games in 2020. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • Google’s Dark Web Report used to be the only consumer-focused platform that let owners scan major data breaches, dark web marketplaces, and private forums to see if their personal information had ended up in the hands of hackers.
  • Industry observers note that google claims it sunsetted Dark Web Report because, although the information it provided was generally useful, the service failed to provide “helpful next steps” for owners whose data was found on the dark web.
  • Dark Web Report may not have been perfect, but it was the only early warning system of its kind that was available for personal use and let owners run scans free of cost.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google’s Dark Web Report used to be the only consumer-focused platform that let owners scan major data breaches, dark web marketplaces, and private forums to see if their personal information had ended up in the hands of hackers. But the firm discontinued the service at the start of 2026, with newly introduced scans stopping on Jan. 15 and all accounts deleted on Feb. 16.

Industry observers note that google claims it sunsetted Dark Web Report because, although the information it provided was generally useful, the service failed to provide “helpful next steps” for owners whose data was found on the dark web. Google promised a new service that would provide more actionable intel, but that service has yet to materialize, and there haven’t been any further announcements about it yet.

Dark Web Report may not have been perfect, but it was the only early warning system of its kind that was available for personal use and let owners run scans free of cost. Now that it’s gone, however, there are plenty of other services that offer the same service at varying costs and levels of effectiveness. Let’s talk through the nature of the insight that Google's reports offered, how it collected that information in the first place, and what options exist in the market to replace it.

Google introduced the Dark Web Report in March 2023 as a premium feature available to Google One customers, but later extended it for free to anyone with a Google account and moved it to the "Results about you" dashboard.

Recent findings suggest that you'd set up a monitoring profile with your name, date of birth, physical address, phone number, emails, and Social Security Number if you lived in the U.S. After that, you could head to the dashboard anytime you wanted to run a free scan across dark web forums and marketplaces, publicly disclosed corporate data breaches, and other hidden online spaces to see if any of your personal information had shown up there. It was easy to use—but not a lot of people knew it existed in the first place.

Recent findings suggest that it’s unclear what prompted the internal decision at Google, but in the absence of concrete next steps, it is reasonable to think the reports could create panic for the uninitiated. There’s no way to remove your information from the dark web once it’s already in circulation there. Still, having an early warning so you could reset 2FA or self-lock your SSN isn’t without merit.

According to recent reports, but perhaps more importantly, most people with Google accounts didn’t know and hadn’t heard of the Dark Web Report’s existence. Google has likely taken it as a hint that owners want more active remediation tools than simple alerts, which is why it’s now directing users to the Password Manager, Passkeys, and “Results about you” dashboard instead—though, again, the company hasn't followed through on a direct replacement for Dark Web Report, despite teasing such a feature.

Many of the top dark web scanners draw from the same well of information, scanning against major data breaches and dark web spaces. Several also offer breach notifications that send you email alerts when your details show up in a periodic scan. However, none of that is worth paying for because Have I Been Pwned or Mozilla Monitor cover those features quite well for free. Even the default password managers from Google and Apple come with some ability to monitor leaked credentials.

There isn’t an easy way to scrub your information from the dark web once it ends up getting leaked. But you can take steps to protect sensitive information or financial data once you know there’s been a leak. If a password has been compromised, reset it immediately. Also, enable 2FA on the affected account for added security. Even better, switch to a passkey if that account supports it. If not, authenticator apps are a safer way to receive 2FA codes than standard SMS.

It has been revealed that if your Social Security number has been leaked, freeze your credit with Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion. You can do this by contacting each agency separately. Freezing your credit will prevent unauthorized credit withdrawals and protect your credit score from abuse by attackers. If one of your credit or debit card numbers has ended up in a breach, call your bank to freeze transactions on that card immediately.

Recent findings suggest that finally, get in the habit of using email aliases instead of sharing your actual email address with every platform and service provider. Addy.io and Proton’s SimpleLogin are both popular services that let you generate temporary email aliases that point to your inbox.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that world of Warcraft: Forever's player vs. player systems will work much differently than in previous versions of old-school WoW, developer Blizzard has revealed. While Forever is now out in the wild and breaking records from the MMORPG, how its PvP rank system would work remained largely a mystery prior to launch. Now, Blizzard has shared more information about how players will earn PvP ranks and honor, with the main takeaway being that players won't have to commit to months of grinding or competing with players on their own faction for top ranks. Honor, a currency earned from killing enemy players and completing battlegrounds and PvP activities, will now exclusively be used to purchase PvP gear and doesn't impact progress towards ranks. Instead, players will rank points by completing daily and weekly PvP quests, fighting in open-world PvP activities like the Gurabashi Arena, and competing in the weekly battleground. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VDNmrrB2k2w In a video detailing the latest system, Blizzard said the rank climb will now feel "more varied and predictable" than in the past, when players needed to farm varying amounts of Honor to rank up based on how other players on their same faction were performing. It will also encourage players to engage in different PvP activities each week, instead of simply doing the most efficient one in terms of Honor gained. Though it isn't central to ranking up, Honor still remains as a currency and is used to purchase  PvP gear. Players can start purchasing PvP gear at lower ranks, and then use Honor to upgrade those items into epics once they've reached higher ranks. At the max rank of 14, players unlock access to epic weapons equal in power to gear from the MMO's endgame raids. Blizzard said the biggest way to progress the ranks is by completing weekly season journey quests. For those who might be unable to play for a few weeks and worry about falling behind, each weekly quest doesn't disappear and can be completed later in the season. Forever's PvP rank grind will still take several months of dedicated play (according to Blizzard, players can expect to hit max rank by week eight or nine of a season), but the amount of actual time required will be far less. That's thanks to players on the same faction no longer competing to farm the most Honor in order to achieve top ranks, something that resulted in players of original WoW and WoW Classic grinding battlegrounds for 12 or more hours a day for months on end. "WoW: Forever's Honor system keeps you coming back each week, rather than grinding every day," Blizzard said. "We hope this is a more approachable system that still provides a healthy challenge as you climb to max rank." This isn't the first time Blizzard has revamped classic WoW's Honor system. Though it kept the infamous old system in place for WoW Classic's launch in 2019, it finally made changes in 2023. It kept the Honor grind somewhat intact, but removed the competition between players on the same faction, instead requiring players meet certain Honor thresholds each week to rank up. Forever looks to be a hit for Blizzard so far, with more than 15 million characters created and a record breaking number of concurrent, returning, and weekly players. Despite the game's massive launch and a banner year for WoW in general, it wasn't enough to snag the MMO a nomination for Best Ongoing Game at The Game Awards. In other Forever news, Blizzard recently hotfixed a major dungeon exploit that saw some players, including prominent streamers, earn thousands of gold, only for Blizzard to then remove the ill-gotten gains and glitch temporary account suspensions to the worst offenders.

Forever's PvP rank grind will still take several months of dedicated play (according to Blizzard, players can expect to hit max rank by week eight or nine of a season), but the amount of actual time required will be far less. "WoW: Forever's Honor system keeps you coming back each week, rather than grinding every day," Blizzard mentioned. "We hope this is a more approachable system that still provides a healthy challenge as you climb to max rank.".

The Princess of Wales touched down in India this Monday for a whirlwind three-day visit to the country with her husband, Prince William.

According to recent reports, the couple visited Mumbai for the sixth Earthshot Prize Summit, which took place on Tuesday. It marked the Waleses’ first joint overseas visit since Catherine’s cancer diagnosis.

The busy schedule of engagements kicked off with a game of gully cricket—an informal version of the game played on the street. For the occasion, the Princess of Wales struck a balance between polished and casual, opting for crisp white Alexander McQueen trousers, paired with a white top layered under a pistachio blazer by Veronica Beard.

The Princess of Wales debuted a pistachio blazer by Veronica Beard for the outing.

The finishing touch? A matching set of green amethyst earrings and a drop necklace from one of Catherine’s favorite jewelry labels, Kiki McDonough. Catherine has at least 20 pairs of earrings from the jeweler, ranging from the blue topaz drops she wore to Royal Ascot to the green tourmaline, green amethyst and diamond earrings set in gold, designed specially for her to mark Princess Charlotte’s birth.

The apple green amethysts, which she wore in Mumbai, are among the lesser-seen designs in her collection but proved the perfect accessory for this first engagement.

While in Mumbai, the prince’s program focused on The Earthshot Prize and its mission to accelerate solutions to the world’s most pressing environmental challenges. The princess joined the prince for a number of engagements during the visit.

The Prince and Princess of Wales in Mumbai on Monday.

During their time in Mumbai, the prince and princess also celebrated several of the deep cultural connections between the United Kingdom and India: cricket, fashion, and cinema.

Beginning with an engagement focused on the uniquely Indian passion of gully cricket andconcluding with a visit to the heart of Mumbai’s film industry, their royal highnessescelebrated the creativity, talent, and cultural influence that continue to shape modern India andstrengthen ties between the two countries.

The highlight of the visit was the Earthshot Prize ceremony on Tuesday, November 17. Five Earthshot leaders were given 1 million euros (about $1.1 million USD) to accelerate the impact of their innovative solutions. Mumbai made perfect sense as the host city; India is home to more Earthshot Prize winners and finalists than any other country.

The Princess of Wales looked elegant in a lime green blazer layered over an all-white ensemble.

Recent findings suggest that since founding the prize in 2020, Prince William has attended all of the awards ceremonies: in London, Boston, Singapore, Cape Town, and Rio de Janeiro. Catherine joined the prince in London in 2021 and again in Boston the following year, but has missed recent editions in the further corners of the globe. This was partly due to the princess’s restricted work schedule while she underwent treatment for cancer and spent time in recovery.

It marked a return to the country for Prince William and Kate, who carried out a state visit in April 2016. The week-long tour saw the then Duke and Duchess of Cambridge explore Mumbai, Newly introduced Delhi, Assam, and Bhutan, racking up a total of 22 engagements that saw them try their hand at cricket, meet Bollywood stars and royalty, and champion charitable causes close to their hearts.

It was one of four overseas trips taken by the couple that year. Although William and Kate still travel, it is with far less frequency as the couple prioritizes a stable family life. Their last major overseas tour was to the Caribbean in 2022.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SPOILERS AHEAD for The End of Oak Street, now streaming with a HBO Max subscription.

One of the biggest “shock” sounds I’ve made while in a movie theater this year has been for The End of Oak Street. I knew the Spielberg-inspired science fiction movie would have dinosaurs and probably some wild twists, but I really wasn’t expecting Greg’s death. I just found out that what happens after the dino chomps him up was originally much different.

Recent findings suggest that the End of Oak Street feels like one of those rare family-oriented sci-fi flicks we don’t see enough anymore. So, I was very surprised when Ewan McGregor’s character dies in front of his wife and kids. It was completely heartbreaking to watch – especially right after that kinky dino scene. It really darkened the tone of the whole movie. But, as it turns out, it was originally even darker. Crazy, right? As Anne Hathaway revealed to Entertainment Weekly:.

Greg always died in the script, but in the original movie that I signed up for, he didn’t come back. And that was something that got changed very close to the start of filming. I have to give all credit to David and J.J. because they had total faith that it was the right thing to do. And they kept turning to me and I was like, ‘Guys, I was so invested in the other version. I have no way of knowing this. I’m just trusting you that this is the right thing to do.’.

Now, I didn’t think Greg was going to come back when I watched the movie, because how could he? Once what’s left of the Platt family goes through the portal and realises they’ve travelled back in time, I was so happy with what happened next. Denise calls her husband to deliver a pizza, and he does just in time to be outside the radius of Oak St.

It has been revealed that sure, the logic for the ending is a tad janky, but I needed that feel-good conclusion (along with the dog not dying either, of course). To me, the movie is only about dinosaurs on the surface. The more interesting part is the dynamic between the Platt family. At the beginning of it, Denise and Greg are clearly having some marital problems, and Denise feels resentful and stagnant with her husband. But they start to find their way back to each other while in crisis. And then she sees him take charge of their family by defending them – even though he sadly dies in the process. It’s the weird, twisted sci-fi family therapy they somehow all needed.

Hathaway has also shared her love of the ending of The End of Oak Street, too. In her words:.

When I saw the movie, I saw it with someone who had lost their father, and they burst into tears at the ending. They said, ‘Actually, it’s just what I want from a movie like this, and it could only happen in a movie, and I love it.’ And so I just want to give my absolute credit and hats off to J.J. and David for coming up with that ending.

Sources indicate that sure, characters often need to die in movies, but not in this one. I love Hathaway’s anecdote about how Greg coming back to life positively affected one viewer. The ending adds a bit of wish fulfilment and helps even out the tone of the whole experience. Look, if the end is going to include two Jeannettes by the end, Greg can live too! I'm so happy he did.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's already clear that Grand Theft Auto 6 has a very different timbre than most other GTA games. While criminal hijinks and acerbic satire remain part of the experience, it's also much more interested in portraying characters and relationships in a more convincing, human fashion.

Industry observers note that one of the most striking examples of this is its depiction of co-protagonist Jason Duval, who, unlike the vast majority of GTA's main characters, is often notable for what he doesn't say rather than what he does. According to Rockstar's senior vice president of narrative Rupert Humphries, Jason's laconic nature was inspired by a personality type observed in both cinema and real-life.

"When we decided we wanted to tell a story about a couple on the run, we looked at all the similar kinds of movies, and one of the ones that really stood out was [Sam] Peckinpah's The Getaway" Humphries explained in a statement given to Destructoid (via GamesRadar). Steve McQueen was famous for pulling lines out of scripts and saying things with his presence alone. We wanted to see how close we could get to that with a game character, where so many of our protagonists have been the opposite.".

Humphries notes this also "resonated" with research the studio was doing around Army veterans, particularly Army Rangers. In Grand Theft Auto 6, Duval is a veteran of the game's equivalent military organisation called the Marauders. "These guys typically aren't running their mouths or reacting to something unless it's strictly necessary, while still being strong and still asserting themselves," Humphries explained.

Industry observers note that establishing a more grounded character was not solely a directive for Jason. It was a goal of the writing more broadly. This is interesting considering Florida was picked as the setting for GTA 6 in-part due to the wild 'Florida Man' stories that circulate on the Internet from the state. "Researching the prolific and headline-grabbing criminal activity that had been taking place over decades in Florida was an obvious starting point," game writer Michael Wiafe pointed out.

According to recent reports, "From then on, it was about coming up with authentic characters that didn't stray too far from reality but also were not totally bound by it either," Wiafe continues. "The majority of our main characters are undeniably reprehensible on paper, full-blown criminals, but also decent human beings. Their moral makeup isn’t necessarily cut-and-dry, and we don’t attempt to make excuses for them. What's crucial is how they resonate, no matter where you're experiencing the game in the world.".

According to recent reports, this is just one of the things that makes Rockstar's latest crime sim a marvel on pretty much all fronts. And while us PC gamers will have to wait an unspecified amount of time before it arrives on the platform, you can bet it going to be quite the experience when it does.

#108716. You Can Play Grand Theft Auto 6 At 60fps Using This Absurdly Complicated Method

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1224 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gamespot ↗ Open Full Page

You Can Play Grand Theft Auto 6 At 60fps Using This Absurdly Complicated Method

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1224 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, grand Theft Auto VI is finally out for consoles, and it's every bit the visual showcase of the generation that it was promising to be since its reveal.
  • Grand Theft Auto VI is finally out for consoles, and it's every bit the visual showcase of the generation that it was promising to be since its reveal.
  • Irrespective of what platform you play on, Grand Theft Auto VI is limited to 30fps.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, grand Theft Auto VI is finally out for consoles, and it's every bit the visual showcase of the generation that it was promising to be since its reveal. You'll struggle to find a better-looking game on the current generation of hardware, but one concession Rockstar had to make to achieve that was limiting its frame rate--a limitation some players are going to absurd lengths to overcome. Irrespective of what platform you play on, Grand Theft Auto VI is limited to 30fps. Doubling that to the more desirable 60fps is something current console hardware just isn't capable of with this level of visual fidelity and simulation, which means you'll have to rely on other methods of frame generation to get there. That's the idea that underpins technology like Veyra: an open-source real-time video enhancer that uses your PC and HDMI 2.1 capture card to bring frame generation to your console. It's a...complicated process. First you'll need a capable capture card (like one of the many from Elgato) that is able to ingest gameplay at 4K over HDMI 2.1. You'll need to connect that to your PC using certified USB-C 3.2 data cable, which needs to plug into a suitable motherboard with True USB 3.2 Gen 2 support. On the pricier end of the requirements, you will need a relatively powerful GPU, with the creators recommending a RTX-40 or newer card from Nvidia in order to tap into the card's Tensor cores (that are used for frame generation on PC). Pair that with an OLED monitor, which is also strongly recommended thanks to its near-instant pixel response times, and you've got everything you need to finally enjoy Grand Theft Auto VI (and more) at higher frame rates. Veyra is able to take gameplay captured on your console and apply a variety of enhancements over the footage, which is ultimately displayed (and played) through the PC you're capturing the footage to. You can utilize upscaling and frame generation techniques from Nvidia, AMD, and Intel to enhance both the resolution and perceived fluidity of your console games this way, with as minimal latency as possible. Given all the parts in the chain, from your console, to the capture card, and through to your PC, escaping any additional latency is impossible. But Verya is seemingly built with mitigating latency as its highest priority, and seems to achieve that based on feedback from some consumers on Reddit. Is it worth it to go through this much hassle to play GTA 6 at 60fps? If you have all the required hardware then it's at least worth a shot, even just for the sake of curiosity. But actually investing in a setup to achieve this is probably overkill. For starters, it requires a PC that will probably be capable enough to play Rockstar's latest sequel at or on-par with the console version once it does land on PC (which will reportedly be sooner than you think). Capture cards are not outrageously expensive, but they're also not free, which can also be stated for all the high-quality cables you'll need between each of the three required devices. I admit, I admire the dedication to playing Grand Theft Auto VI at launch in the best possible way, but I would wager that you're likely going to be spending a lot more time troubleshooting some incompatibility somewhere along this chain of dependencies instead of enjoying the game itself. Still, if you're curious you can find a lot of detailed information about what this setup requires and why, and determine for yourself if it's worth the price to cruise around Leonida with a bit more fluidity.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kim Zolciak’s daughter Brielle Biermann is officially a married woman.

In a recent development, the influencer and former Don’t Be Tardy star married baseball player Billy Seidl in front of a group of close family and friends in Naples, Florida, on Saturday, November 21. Brielle shared footage of herself and her husband in their wedding attire, as waves rolled in on a nearby beach.

“Mrs. Seidl,” Brielle captioned the clip.

Brielle wore a traditional white, flowing wedding dress with a large black bow adorning the left side of the gown while Seidl opted for a traditional tuxedo with a black bowtie. Zolciak was reportedly in attendance with her boyfriend, Kyle Mowitz, per TMZ.

Brielle’s sister Ariana Biermann was one of many to wish the couple congratulations, writing in Instagram comment section, “I’m crying. I love you so much.”.

The bride’s former stepdad, Kroy Biermann, was reportedly absent at the Naples, Florida, wedding as he did not receive an invitation. Also absent was Brielle’s half-brother KJ Biermann amid his legal troubles. (Twins Kaia and Kane were reportedly absent as well.).

Months before the ceremony, Brielle was able to enjoy a bachelorette weekend with her closest friends, including sister Ariana.

Recent findings suggest that “God forbid I have some fun before becoming mrs. 🎀 ,” Brielle wrote via Instagram on August 13 after celebrating in Turks & Caicos.

One month later, Brielle gathered with family and friends for a bridal shower.

“Can’t believe my baby is getting married 🤭🙈 to the most incredible man @bseidl21 ❤️,” Zolciak wrote via Instagram at the time.

Despite some happy celebrations, Brielle and her family have also been embroiled in scandal after her brother Kroy “KJ” Biermann Jr. was arrested for aggravated sodomy and aggravated sexual assault on August 17. (His lawyer has denied all charges.).

Although KJ was released from a youth detention center in September, a judge’s ruling orders the high school student to wear an electronic ankle monitor under 24-hour house arrest.

“The allegations being made against my son are nothing short of reckless and deeply troubling. He categorically denies ever being involved with this woman or engaging in the conduct she has alleged,” Zolciak noted in a statement to Us days after the arrest. “My son voluntarily took a polygraph examination regarding these allegations and passed. Additionally, an examination was conducted, and no DNA belonging to my son was found.”.

On Thursday (November 21), court documents obtained by Us confirmed that KJ’s accuser “will be made available to testify at trial and be subject to cross-examination.” Earlier in the week, Georgia prosecutors opposed a motion by KJ’s lawyers to have his case moved to juvenile court on the grounds that the teen demonstrated “sophistication and premeditation” in his alleged assault.

It has been revealed that “This behavior has become part of a deeply troubling pattern when it comes to this defendant forcing sexual compliance through a personal relationship,” the docs read. “This defendant has proven to be beyond the rehabilitation offered within the Fulton County Juvenile Court process.”.

Regardless of any drama going on in her family, Brielle has remained focused on her love story with Seidl.

One year after the pair confirmed their relationship status, Seidl proposed to Brielle in Arizona.

“Forever with you 🤍🥹🫀🫶🏻,” Brielle wrote via Instagram in February 2024 with photos from the romantic moment.

Tech Report: Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth Is in a Battle for His Own Survival at the Pentagon

⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the day after the midterm elections, President Donald Trump met with Susie Wiles in the Oval Office.
  • It has been revealed that hegseth was in a precarious position.
  • In the Wednesday meeting, according to a senior White House official, Wiles made clear that the war, the uncertainty of its next steps, and the inflation it had fueled all contributed to the midterms debacle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the day after the midterm elections, President Donald Trump met with Susie Wiles in the Oval Office. He asked his chief of staff whether she believed Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth would survive the impeachment attempt that would soon be launched by a member of his own party.

It has been revealed that hegseth was in a precarious position. He had been among the most aggressive champions of the war with Iran, widely seen as the policy most responsible for the shellacking Republicans had taken the night before. Wiles remained officially supportive of Hegseth throughout her time in the White House, but she had harbored concerns about the secretary from the start. She did not believe he was forthright about his skeletons during a rocky confirmation process, and she considered the subsequent Signalgate scandal an amateurish disaster.

In the Wednesday meeting, according to a senior White House official, Wiles made clear that the war, the uncertainty of its next steps, and the inflation it had fueled all contributed to the midterms debacle. She offered her resignation, but Trump declined. On Thursday night, in a contentious meeting in the Oval Office, she offered to resign again. Trump revealed the next day that Wiles would leave the White House for his outside political operation.

Industry observers note that hegseth’s fate was still uncertain. A deeply unpopular figure among the American public, presiding over an even more unpopular war, he faced an impeachment push led by Representative Thomas Massie. “He is just failing,” mentioned Republican senator Thom Tillis of North Carolina—who voted to confirm Hegseth at the start of Trump’s term—in an interview with Vanity Fair. “In the same way that Kristi Noem failed at Homeland Security, he simply doesn’t have the instincts or the prior experience as an executive that is necessary for this particular role.”.

In a recent development, the secretary of defense has now embarked on a campaign to save his job, and Stephen Miller’s elevation to replace Wiles as Trump’s chief of staff has helped to ensure a reprieve. Trump has so far backed Hegseth publicly, and last week, House Republicans blocked the impeachment effort. “Pete is a fighter,” the White House official explained. “Trump likes fighters.” And there are other reasons to keep him in place, the official said: Confirming a replacement will not be easy, particularly when Democrats take control of Congress, and ousting Hegseth would signal an admission that at this point, Trump’s war is a failure.

According to recent reports, it was the president’s taste for staffers out of central casting that helped put Hegseth—a weekend morning television host with no experience in government, but with the square jaw of an Army Wives extra—in charge of the Department of Defense. He has relied on his talents before the cameras, and a team of advisers attuned to the production of his persona, to both keep his job and sell Trump on aggressive military action from the Pacific to the Persian Gulf. His survival has depended in part on his ability to project strength—not to the public, or to the rank-and-file, but to the president.

“In just under two years, Secretary Hegseth has worked side-by-side with President Trump to restore American power on the world stage, build the strongest military in generations, and instill a warrior ethos at the Pentagon,” White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales said in a statement. “President Trump and Secretary Hegseth have taken bold, necessary action to deny the Iranian regime the ability to develop a nuclear weapon, bring narco-terrorist Nicolas Maduro to American justice, and defend our homeland from dangerous terrorists and cartels—saving American lives.”.

“They will stand behind him in the short term,” said a second senior administration official. And yet, “He is a cost. He’s constantly requiring people to spend political capital on him. The White House is constantly having to come in and save him. The question is, at what point is it too much of a cost to the president?”.

According to recent reports, the morning after Hegseth survived the impeachment attempt, he attended a Veterans Day ceremony at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. Hegseth was joined at the sacred memorial by his closest aides: Jennifer Hegseth, his third wife and a former Fox News producer who serves as an informal but influential adviser; his chief of staff Ricky Buria, a Marine Corps veteran who followed an unusual path into the top brass; and Tami Radabaugh, another former Fox News producer whom Hegseth hired as a senior adviser.

It has been revealed that as the group posed for photos at the Tomb, they chatted and laughed loudly. A US Army sentinel guarding the memorial turned to the group and shouted out a reprimand: “All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times.” After video of the moment made for embarrassing headlines, Hegseth awarded the soldier a Joint Service Commendation Medal and posed alongside several Army officers for a photoshoot that was posted on his social media accounts. The Pentagon did not elaborate on why a soldier was awarded a medal for an act as pedestrian as scolding noisy attendees at a memorial. “Hegseth would not have given him that award had the incident not been on TV,” stated a former senior defense official.

The small group of advisers beside Hegseth has helped the secretary weather a series of scandals in his two years as defense secretary using stage-managed displays of toughness. “He’s a cross between a carnival barker and a personal trainer,” noted John Ullyot, who served as chief Pentagon spokesperson and senior adviser to Hegseth until he left the department last year. A loyal Trump backer, Ullyot initially supported Hegseth’s calls to restore standards and excise identity politics from the military. He has since emerged as a fierce public critic and now believes Hegseth should resign.

In his new book, The President Deserves Better, Ullyot describes a secretary of defense fixated on self-promotion and content creation. Jennifer plays an instrumental role in those efforts, directing the secretary’s social media and a small battalion of accounts that support him online. “It was as if she was producing him in his role as Secretary,” Ullyot writes. She has helped produce—and starred in—dramatic videos of Hegseth posted by the Pentagon’s official social media accounts. “Her entire job is to make his image,” one source told Vanity Fair.

House Republican Thomas Massie, who brought the articles of impeachment against Hegseth last week, argued the bombing was “the result of systemic deterioration and removal of Department of Defense infrastructure that Congress had mandated by law to limit collateral damage to civilians.”.

It has been revealed that her role extended well beyond production, alarming senior officials in the Department of Defense. She interviewed candidates for Pentagon roles. She attended sensitive bilateral meetings with foreign officials. She was included in Signal chats that discussed the war plans for the Houthi operation in Yemen. The former defense official said they warned Hegseth about his wife’s involvement in Pentagon affairs. “She did not have a fucking clearance,” they said. “She shouldn’t be privy to this shit.”.

Hegseth himself seemed too smitten to care. He covered the walls of his office, as well as other meeting rooms and corridors throughout the Pentagon, with large photos of himself and his wife. When The New York Times examined Jennifer’s influence at the department over the summer, Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell called the former cable news producer “an accomplished leader.” He added that the Pentagon “not only welcomes her current leadership but actively aims to involve her even more deeply in the future.” Politico later reported that while advising the secretary of defense, Jennifer was being paid for consulting work by Watchtower Strategies, a Washington lobbying shop that counts Lockheed Martin as a client.

She wasn’t the only Fox News producer at the Pentagon. Hegseth also gave Radabaugh—a former producer on Fox & Friends Weekend with no government experience—broad authority over department affairs, I’m told. Radabaugh made sure that glamorous photos and videos of Hegseth were published online promptly, sometimes scolding aides for taking too long to post. In the first few months of Hegseth’s tenure, she ordered Ullyot to turn a room just off the briefing room into a makeup studio.

“This was ridiculous. I mentioned not only no, but hell no,” Ullyot writes. He warned that news of the makeup studio would leak. “How exactly did a makeup studio fit into the warrior ethos?”.

Recent findings suggest that in response to a detailed list of questions, Pentagon spokesman Joel Valdez declined to answer many of them but emailed a lengthy statement criticizing Ullyot. “There is no ‘makeup studio’ in the Pentagon, and it never existed,” Valdez stated, going on to call Ullyot “a skinwalker,” a “sour puss coward,” and “generally a stupid person” who left “his job in disgrace.” (According to information reviewed by Vanity Fair, Hegseth praised Ullyot after his departure from the Pentagon and offered to recommend him to Susie Wiles, then Trump’s chief of staff.).

“I volunteered to help stand up the Secretary’s press operation for a few months at the start of his term,” Ullyot told Vanity Fair in response. “I left as planned, and the Secretary thanked me for my work. My record over more than 30 years, including as a senior spokesman in the Senate and in the Trump White House, speaks for itself.”.

It has been revealed that hegseth was bullish on the war with Iran from the start. “There weren’t any real cheerleaders for the war in the cabinet outside of Pete Hegseth,” said the second official. “It was Pete and [US Ambassador to Israel] Mike Huckabee.”.

According to recent reports, soon after his confirmation, Hegseth moved to increase his powers and consolidate control over the Pentagon. He ousted generals and subjected senior staff to polygraph tests to weed out leakers, a crusade that resulted in the abrupt firings of top officials that demoralized staff. He tapped Tim Parlatore, his personal lawyer, as a special adviser and charged him with overseeing leak investigations. Parlatore continued to run his own private practice as a criminal defense attorney, and Politico reported this week that while serving as Hegseth’s top adviser, he is representing the son of a Libyan warlord accused of extrajudicial killings and torture.

In keeping with the president’s broad campaign for retribution, Hegseth ordered an investigation into retired Joint Chiefs Chairman General Mark Milley, who had clashed with Trump during his first term, and stripped the four-star general of his security detail. The Pentagon is now working on a newly introduced report on the 2021 Kabul Airport attack, during which 13 American soldiers and 170 Afghan civilians were killed in a suicide bombing during the withdrawal from Afghanistan. At the time, Milley served as chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. The new assessment, one source familiar with the investigation noted, is expected by the end of the month and is intended to serve as a predicate to strip Milley of his four-star rank.

Hegseth waged a parallel war on the press, starting with an attempt to ban NBC News correspondent Courtney Kube from the Pentagon. In a meeting with his advisers, Ullyot writes, Hegseth explained that he and his wife Jennifer were “angry” at Kube for how much she covered his turbulent confirmation process before Congress. “I thought this was loony tunes,” Ullyot writes. One source told me that after NBC News was kicked out of its Pentagon office, Hegseth aides took a full-length mirror from the vacated room and installed it in his makeup studio.

As Hegseth purged senior officials, he grew closer to Buria. The relationship was confounding to many inside the building: Hegseth has pushed to cleanse the Pentagon of ideological diversity, yet he elevated Buria, a holdover from the Biden administration who had previously donated to Democrats. But Buria had earned the trust of Jennifer. When explaining to advisers why he was elevated, Hegseth said he prayed about the decision with his wife. “And you know what? Jen indicates he’s really good with the kids,” Hegseth told them.

Industry observers note that buria was by Hegseth’s side throughout the Signalgate scandal, which, according to several administration officials, was a turning point for the secretary. “Every problem he is having in one way or another goes back to Signalgate,” the second Trump official said. “His extremely hostile relations with the press, his paranoia, his firing of certain people, denied promotions to generals. It was all around paranoia related to Signalgate.”.

“There’s two versions of Hegseth,” remarked a second former defense official. “There is the pre-Signalgate version and the post-Signalgate version. It’s like Jekyll and Hyde. He was Dr. Jekyll until around Signalgate, and he’s been Mr. Hyde ever since. He’s just not making good decisions.”.

It was an almost unbelievable incident: Hegseth shared war intends for a bombing campaign against the Houthis in Yemen on at least two Signal group chats, including one that inadvertently included Jeffrey Goldberg, the editor in chief of The Atlantic.

This was the first major military engagement of Hegseth’s tenure, but he chose to survey the operation with Buria from a temporary secure facility at his Fort McNair home rather than make the short trip to the Pentagon or the White House Situation Room. The decision alarmed some at the Pentagon. “It’s your first major military operation,” stated the second senior Trump official. “Why would you monitor it from your shitty SCIF in your basement? Why not go 10 minutes to the Pentagon where you have the joint staff?”.

“You would think with kinetic operations going on in the Middle East that could have dramatic consequences for service members, that he’d be in the office,” Tillis mentioned.

Trump has so far backed Hegseth publicly, and last week, House Republicans blocked the impeachment effort. “Pete is a fighter,” the White House official explained. “Trump likes fighters.”.

It has been revealed that during Hegseth’s confirmation process, allegations of heavy drinking concerned Republican lawmakers he needed to vote in favor of his nomination. At the time, several Republican senators remarked he promised them he would stop boozing if confirmed. He affirmed this pledge publicly: “This is the biggest deployment of my life,” he told Megyn Kelly in a 2024 interview, “and there won’t be a drop of alcohol on my lips while I’m doing it.”.

Whether or not Hegseth has actually quit drinking continues to be a source of palace intrigue. One official recalled watching Hegseth drink what the secretary suggested were two cocktails—though the official conceded he hadn’t seen the drinks poured, and raised a theory that Hegseth might have been testing whether he would leak the incident to the press. “This was at a time of peak paranoia,” the official stated.

Industry observers note that buria was known to drink on official trips; the official recalled Hegseth’s aide handing out shots to passengers on a US government jet during a Pentagon junket. Two other officials stated Buria would often brag about drinking with Hegseth, including on an official trip to Panama in 2025. The New York Post later reported that Buria had made up a story about him and Hegseth donning disguises to go out and drink, all in an effort to weed out leakers. One of the officials told me they believed the leak claim was Buria’s retroactive effort to cover up that he was boasting about drinking with the secretary.

According to recent reports, “The drinking is what they’re really afraid of,” the second official noted. When asked directly if Hegseth continued drinking as secretary, a Defense Department spokesperson who declined to be named said in a statement: “No, the Secretary has kept his promise that he made during his confirmation hearings and has not drank since becoming Secretary of War.”.

It has been revealed that jennifer and Pete Hegseth have forged a close relationship with Stephen Miller and his wife Katie, their neighbors on a placid and heavily fortified army base south of the White House. Hegseth’s temporary salvation comes thanks in part to support from Miller, who values his deference to Trump. “Stephen doesn’t like all the Liberace shit, the cucaracha shit,” noted the first former official. “Pete right now is fresh out of friends, and misery loves company. But don’t get it twisted. At any moment, at any second, Stephen will cut Pete’s throat.”.

The secretary of defense has made few friends in Washington. One source recalled attending a holiday party stocked with members of the administration during which Hegseth spent much of his time alone in the corner of the room. “Even Kash Patel had people coming up to him to talk,” the source stated. “Pete was alone and isolated. He looked depressed. And this was before the Iran war. His stock has not gone up since then.”.

Recent findings suggest that hegseth has channeled much of his effort into appealing to an audience of one, telling advisers he only cares about Trump’s opinion. “The one thing he’s been successful at, and I think it’s the only thing, is flattering Donald Trump constantly,” the former official stated.

The purpose of this flattery campaign extends beyond keeping his current job. In private, Hegseth has confided in several officials about his ambitions to run for president. This jockeying has exacerbated tensions with Vice President JD Vance. The relationship was already strained by Vance’s private opposition to the Iran war, and it deteriorated significantly after the vice president’s close friend, Dan Driscoll, was pushed out of his position as Army Secretary in August following months of friction with Hegseth.

When explaining to advisers why Buria was elevated, Hegseth said he prayed about the decision with his wife. “And you know what? Jen claims he’s really good with the kids,” Hegseth told them.

“Secretary Hegseth and Vice President Vance share an outstanding working relationship grounded in deep mutual respect and alignment,” Parnell said in a statement to Vanity Fair.

Jennifer has worked in tandem with her husband to push allies on social media and in the press to promote the idea of a presidential run. “She wants to be first lady,” the former official remarked of Jennifer. “She wants to be Hillary.” After the midterms, online influencers whom Hegseth hired earlier this year to work as special government employees at the Pentagon began pitching Hegseth for president. These influencers were nominally hired to promote Hegseth’s efforts to bring war colleges in line with the “warrior ethos,” but in reality they coordinated with Jennifer and Radabaugh on “shitposting,” the second official said. Earlier this month, they rallied to Hegseth’s defense as he came under fire for the Republican ballot box-bloodbath, posting action shots of the secretary with the caption: “STAND. FIGHT. DEFEND THE REPUBLIC.”.

In a recent development, these influencers often attack journalists who cover the Pentagon. In response to a recent story by Politico’s Daniel Lippman, an active-duty Army officer known as InfantryDort on social media—whom Hegseth hired as one of these shadow spokespeople—posted: “I expect you all to ratio the fuck out of this retard and in short order. Daniel Lippman remains absolute journalistic filth.” A Politico spokesperson responded: “Daniel is one of Washington’s best-sourced reporters, and we’re lucky to have him at POLITICO.”.

Recent findings suggest that when Democrats take control of Congress, they are expected to focus much of their oversight on Hegseth, including the scandals from his personal life. The subjects broached in his contentious confirmation hearings—including an affidavit signed by his former sister-in-law alleging abuse against his second wife—are likely to be relitigated. (His second wife denied that she was physically abused.).

“Is that going to be good for the president?” Tillis asked. “His entire confirmation will be re-prosecuted. That affidavit will get a lot of attention. Family members will most likely be subpoenaed. Does he really want to go through that at a personal level, and at the same time be such a massive disruption for the leader of the most lethal, complex organization in American government? Is this about Pete, or is this about America’s defense? I don’t know how any objective person can say that the value that he brings is greater than that distraction and the cost of him remaining in place.”.

Industry observers note that “If he had any dignity, he would resign and allow the president to appoint a replacement in the lame duck session,” stated the first official. “But he doesn’t.”.

According to recent reports, hegseth’s ability to project confidence is not confined to the cameras. He was bullish on the war with Iran from the start. “There weren’t any real cheerleaders for the war in the cabinet outside of Pete Hegseth,” noted the second official. “It was Pete and [US Ambassador to Israel] Mike Huckabee.” In late December 2025, Hegseth met with Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu at the Four Seasons in Palm Beach shortly before Netanyahu ventured to Mar-a-Lago to make the case for fresh strikes on Iran. By February, Netanyahu was pushing Trump to join Israel in a full-blown war to topple the Iranian regime.

Hegseth was all-in, his confidence buoyed by the success of Operation Midnight Hammer—a series of strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities in June 2025—and the raid to abduct Venezuelan dictator Nicolás Maduro. His allies in the administration point to these operations, as well as a post-pandemic surge in military recruitment numbers, as his major successes in the job.

Sources indicate that but multiple officials who spoke with Vanity Fair noted they believed that when briefing Trump, Hegseth understated the risks of war with Iran from the beginning and went on to overstate its successes as the conflict dragged on. “Pete gave the rosiest picture in the world,” said the first former official. During early discussions about potentially launching the war, the official said they were struck by how promptly Hegseth started speaking about the operation as a “foregone conclusion.”.

“Leading up into the war, he presented, along with [Central Command Commander Admiral] Brad Cooper, overly optimistic projections of what the air campaign could achieve,” mentioned the second administration official. “This is how the president got this idea that it could be done in a matter of two to three weeks.”.

Hegseth ran against Democrat U.S. Senator Amy Klobuchar in 2012.

Tillis, for his part, remarked that he did not believe Hegseth was forthright with Trump about the war. “He planned the good, bright, shiny stuff that was Epic Fury, but clearly did not brief the president on things that anybody that’s had any experience in the Middle East knows,” Tillis added. “The first thing that goes is the Strait of Hormuz.”.

“Secretary Hegseth and Pentagon leadership consistently provide the President with the complete, unvarnished picture so he can make the best choices for America’s security and success,” Parnell remarked in a statement.

According to recent reports, on the first day of the war, a missile struck the Minab elementary school in southern Iran, killing more than 150 people, the majority of them children. The US military has thus far refused to publicly admit responsibility for the strike, despite a preliminary military investigation concluding within days of the strike that a US missile struck the school. Before the attack, Hegseth gutted the Pentagon program aimed at reducing civilian harm during military operations, ProPublica reported in March. House Republican Thomas Massie, who brought the articles of impeachment against Hegseth last week, argued the bombing was “the result of systemic deterioration and removal of Department of Defense infrastructure that Congress had mandated by law to limit collateral damage to civilians.”.

Massie cast the strike as a consequence of Hegseth’s oft-repeated mantra: “Maximum lethality, not tepid legality.”.

Recent findings suggest that as the war went on, officials said, Hegseth continued to trumpet its successes, showing the president what one official described as “hype videos” depicting strikes on missile launchers, Iranian ships, and old aircraft. Hegseth told Trump “that the majority of Iran’s missile capabilities and the majority of Iran’s Air Force was destroyed,” the official said, even though US intelligence “indicated that wasn’t the case, and that the majority of Iran’s missiles and missile launchers by the end of the major combat phase of the war were still intact.”.

“He creates an echo chamber in the press corps so that he can get only nice questions or do made-for-TV stuff,” noted Senator Tillis.

Hegseth also worked behind the scenes to promote positive media coverage of the war. He briefed Fox News hosts whom he remained friendly with on the war’s progress and encouraged them to present a positive picture on air. But Hegseth himself has made little effort to explain or defend the war to Americans. Even as the war has become a political debacle for the administration, he remains bullish on escalation. “Pete is the only one who wants to restart strikes,” the first official remarked.

According to recent reports, we were all sitting in our assigned seats waiting for the performance to start when a security official walked into the Pentagon briefing room to make an announcement. Hegseth had not held a Pentagon press briefing since May. Now, facing an impeachment effort from a member of his own party, he came before the cameras. “If anyone gets out of line today, you’re going to be physically removed,” the official mentioned. “Is that clear?”.

According to recent reports, “Sense of decorum,” the official said apologetically. “Just be professional.”.

The official said he was just relaying orders from Hegseth’s office. A few minutes later, Joel Valdez, the press aide, walked out and asked if anyone was confused. Everyone was. “I could tell you off the record?” he said. No, the reporters replied. “Do you want to hear it off the record?” No, they said again.

Valdez looked down at his shoes and then walked out of the room without saying another word. “In my 30 years in DC, I have never heard that,” noted a cameraman. “This is crazytown.”.

According to recent reports, at 8 a.m. sharp, Hegseth walked out wearing a loud plaid suit, a striped tie, and an American flag pocket square. The timing is no coincidence; officials said Hegseth schedules briefings in the 8 a.m. hour because Trump is known to watch Fox News at that time.

It has been revealed that the secretary of defense began reading his speech from a stack of papers on the podium. From my assigned seat in the back row, I felt as if I were watching an interpretive dance. The choreography of Hegseth’s hand movements and facial expressions was as slick as his hair, which was gelled into a stiff meringue that moved in unison with his tanned face.

Hegseth punctuated a line about President Trump’s “decisive” leadership with a clenched fist thrust downward. The word “overseeing” was expressed with a slow swipe of the hand over an imaginary stretch of purview. As Hegseth recalled the glories of the Maduro operation—and, parenthetically, his part in directing them—he dismissed criticism of the raid by leaning into the microphone, shaking his head from side to side and wiggling his eyebrows: “It wasn’t”—dramatic pause for eyebrow wiggle—“a kidnapping.”.

Hegseth's presser had a pantomime quality.

The briefing itself exuded little of the confidence Hegseth sought to signal before the cameras. He took seven questions in total, sticking to friendly reporters in the front rows who had signed a pledge in September 2025 to not report “unauthorized information” from the Pentagon. One of them, a representative of Real America’s Voice, asked “what message” is sent to America’s allies when “our own politicians don’t support taking out the narco traffickers that kill their own constituents?” It wasn’t so much a question as a warm bath. Some in the room, visibly frustrated by the waste of time, rolled their eyes. Others shouted questions from the back about Iran and impeachment. Hegseth refused to look at them.

“He creates an echo chamber in the press corps so that he can get only nice questions or do made-for-TV stuff,” stated Tillis, who also decried Hegseth for filming a slick video of himself outside the Department of Defense making the case for why he should not be impeached: “He demonstrated more impulsiveness by using taxpayer dollars to defend himself against impeachment.”.

In his remarks before the press, Hegseth framed the effort to remove him as an attack on the troops. “If they want to come for the warriors, they’re going to have to come through me,” he said, jabbing a finger into his chest. But the impeachment targeted Hegseth, not “the warriors.” We had assembled to hear Pete make the case for Pete. Indeed, he had not held a press briefing when a Navy commander died in a helicopter crash on July 1, or when three US soldiers were killed in an Iranian strike on a base in Jordan on July 17. What brought him back before the cameras was not the ongoing war in the Middle East but his own fight to save his career here in Washington.

The performance earned a rave review from the one viewer who mattered. “Pete Hegseth gets an ‘A’ PLUS, PLUS, PLUS,” Trump wrote on Truth Social.

Early on in Hegseth’s tenure, he confided in advisers about his “biggest fear” as he took on the mighty responsibility of leading the Department of Defense, the first former official told me: “Being fired and embarrassed.” For now, Trump is standing by his secretary. He always is, until he isn’t. When asked just before the midterms whether Wiles would remain on as his chief of staff, Trump stated there was “zero chance” he’d replace her. Three weeks later, she was out.

#108713. Want To Start Lifting Effectively? GTA 6 Is A Good Teacher

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1585 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gamespot ↗ Open Full Page

Want To Start Lifting Effectively? GTA 6 Is A Good Teacher

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1585 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here, and people are discovering all manner of little details in the game that speak to the developer's commitment to realism.
  • According to recent reports, rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here, and people are discovering all manner of little details in the game that speak to the developer's commitment to realism.
  • For starters, Jason has a home gym, and that's just smart on his part.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here, and people are discovering all manner of little details in the game that speak to the developer's commitment to realism. One such detail is the game's weightlifting and general fitness systems, and they seem to be pretty great, so much so that if you're thinking about getting into weight lifting, GTA 6's lessons are a good place to start. For starters, Jason has a home gym, and that's just smart on his part. Not having to leave your house and head to a gym is a godsend for anyone short on time or for those who simply enjoy the solitude of slinging weight around alone. For Jason, it's even better--he lives on the water, and it looks pretty damn serene heading to his workout pad for a sweat. If you're thinking about crafting your own home gym, Jason's setup is exactly what you need to get started: a squat rack, bench, kettlebells, barbells, and iron plates. Garage gym expert Cooper Mitchell also pointed out that Jason's squat stand uses 3"x3" uprights with 1" holes, and that's a great choice by Jason--or you--because it means you have universal support for other attachments from different brands that you might add over time. Jason also has his setup outfitted with horse stall mats, which is another super-smart choice on his part, not only to protect his flooring, but also because they hold up in the outdoor setting that he uses. Having personally invested in horse stall mats for my own home gym, I can vouch for their incredibly sturdy makeup. They are far better than the cheap interlocking styrofoam mats. They cost more and are a massive pain in the ass to get in place due to their weight and structure. But that's just how it is. I am a little concerned about Jason leaving all of this equipment outdoors, considering it rains a lot in Florida and is very humid. This may not be ideal for his iron plates, specifically, or his rack. That being remarked, Jason (and Lucia) can also work out at an indoor gym, so they have their bases covered. Moving beyond the equipment, GTA 6 really nails the details on how to actually build muscle. To maximize your gains, first you need to use proper form. If Jason does not gently lower the bar on chest presses, he fails his reps, and that's basically how it works in real life. Making slow, controlled movements with any free weight is good practice, and it's nice to see the game reinforce this by giving you a fail state when you move the weight too rapidly or in an uncontrolled manner. Of course, you can pack on muscle with bad form and so-called "ego-lifting," but it's generally more advisable to focus on your form. Making light weight feel heavy is the real path to gains. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LfztIWqrJ7s After hitting chest, doing squats, or swinging the kettlebell, GTA 6 encourages you to eat some protein to lock in your gains, and that's also how it works in real life. You can lift all you want, but if you're not eating enough protein, you won't progress optimally. In GTA 6, your protein intake can come in the form of shakes and bars that Jason has at home, or he can head out into the world and grab a bite that way. You also need to rest to feel your best and see the most improvements to your physique in GTA 6, and that's also good advice in real life. When you're in the act of lifting, you're tearing your muscles apart to make them grow back bigger via hypertrophy, but the actual muscle growth happens during rest and sleep. GTA 6 goes even further with its own dedicated fitness app on your phone that tracks your progress and serves as a reminder to stay, as the kids say, locked in. This is great, and another solid replication of the experience you might have with your own fitness app or watch. A word to the wise, though: Do not get too obsessed with tracking your macros and workouts in the game or in your personal life. Life is meant to be lived and enjoyed, even if it means you're not in "optimal" shape. Your health and fitness journey is personal to you. So go eat a donut and drink a beer at the same time like Jason does. You do not need to have 8% body fat like Take-Two's own CEO Strauss Zelnick does. Enjoy your life, in Vice City and out, but if you want some tips on how to get started, GTA 6 offers a solid foundation to build from.

Recent findings suggest that the Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ was a free update to the beloved roguelike that arrived on PC in 2024, but launched on console earlier this week in a head-to-head matchup against Grand Theft Auto 6. The marketing stunt may have been a success, but AI-generated music tracks discovered in a special new Vice City mode have turned the launch into a nightmare.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that google has given its AI-powered "Ask Maps" feature a major upgrade, adding tools for trip planning, real-time route guidance, appointment finding, and saved-list search. The updates begin rolling out today on Android and iOS.

In a recent development, google rolled out Ask Maps last March as an AI assistant designed to handle questions and requests more complicated than simply searching the word "bar" or "groceries." Instead of performing simple keyword searches, the idea behind Ask Maps is that you can describe several specific requirements at once, and Maps will find places that match them all. For example, you could ask for a restaurant with outdoor seating for a certain number of people, and "Ask Maps" will factor in your past searches and give you results. Of course, AI assistants have a habit of making things up, so even with today's roll-out, you'll want to double-check your sources before you drive an hour to the wrong restaurant.

It has been revealed that to me, this is the most useful new feature launching today. Whether you're planning a day trip for holiday shopping or something more ambitious, like a three-day road trip with coastal hikes and oceanfront dining, Ask Maps will put together a day-by-day schedule. Each strategy includes insider tips and numbered map pins for every stop, so you can see the whole route at a glance. Once you're happy with the plan, you can share it with friends and family or export it to Google Docs on desktop.

According to recent reports, when it's time to head out, you can ask Maps to pull up your itinerary, or look for the "itinerary" badge in your chat history. You'll see real-time details such as live traffic conditions, whether a place is currently open, and even the vibe at your next stop.

Plans can change on the fly, too. Ask Maps to add a scenic viewpoint or a lunch spot along the way, then tap to get directions to your next stop straight from the itinerary.

Here's what else you can use Ask Maps to do, starting today.

Pulling up directions now surfaces "Know Before You Go" tips for your route. These include where to park or charge your car, along with real-time conditions like weather, potential delays, and tolls.

Sources indicate that ask Maps is also gaining some agentic capabilities. Allegedly, you can just ask, “Find me a 4 p.m. nail appointment near me,” and Ask Maps will show you open slots across nearby businesses. In addition to finding appointments, Google indicates this agent will be able to call local businesses on your behalf—stay tuned while I wait for the upgrade and test this one out myself.

If you keep lists of saved places, Ask Maps can now search them for you. Ask something like, "Which spots saved in my lists have availability for 5 in the next 30 minutes?" Ask Maps looks across your lists and checks live availability, so you can pick a place and go.

These updates start rolling out today on Android and iOS. Travel itineraries and saved-list search are available everywhere Ask Maps is offered. "Know Before You Go" route tips and appointment finding are launching first in the U.S., with more regions coming soon.
